payload.statement: For the balanced reverse-channel witness \(P^\dagger\), benefit--harm point \(\theta^\dagger\), and entropy budget \(\kappa^\dagger\), one has \(0<\kappa^\dagger<\log2\) and \[\theta^\dagger\in\Phi_3(\mathcal F_{3,\kappa^\dagger}(P^\dagger))\setminus\Phi_2(\mathcal F_{2,\kappa^\dagger}(P^\dagger)).\] Consequently, \[\Phi_2(\mathcal F_{2,\kappa^\dagger}(P^\dagger))\subsetneq\Phi_3(\mathcal F_{3,\kappa^\dagger}(P^\dagger)),\] so three latent states are sometimes necessary for the full benefit--harm image.
payload.proof_tex:
Let \(R=(Y(0),Y(1))\). The proof uses a support-pattern obstruction for a mixture of product distributions and then embeds it in the causal response-type program. Define the balanced reverse-channel law \(P^\dagger\) by
\[
p^\dagger_{00}=p^\dagger_{11}=\frac1{20},
\qquad
p^\dagger_{01}=p^\dagger_{10}=\frac9{20},
\tag{1}
\]
and put
\[
\theta^\dagger=\left(0,\frac9{10}\right),
\qquad
\kappa^\dagger=h\!\left(\frac9{10}\right)+\frac1{10}\log2.
\tag{2}
\]
Every summand in (2) is nonnegative and at least one is positive, so \(\kappa^\dagger>0\). Moreover,
\[
10\kappa^\dagger
=9\log\frac{10}{9}+\log20
=\log\!\left(20\left(\frac{10}{9}\right)^9\right).
\tag{3}
\]
The exact integer inequality
\[
20\cdot10^9=20{,}000{,}000{,}000
<396{,}718{,}580{,}736=2^{10}9^9
\]
and strict monotonicity of the logarithm imply from (3) that \(10\kappa^\dagger<10\log2\). Hence \(0<\kappa^\dagger<\log2\), as required by the declared budget range.

First construct a three-state witness. Index its states by \(00,10,11\), and take
\[
(\pi_{00},\pi_{10},\pi_{11})
=\left(\frac1{20},\frac9{10},\frac1{20}\right),
\qquad
(e_{00},e_{10},e_{11})=\left(0,\frac12,1\right),
\tag{4}
\]
with the response distribution at state \(ij\) degenerate on response type \((i,j)\). Equivalently, take \(W=R\). Conditional on \(W\), the response type is constant, so \(A\perp R\mid W\). Under the causal completion \(Y=R_A\), the state \(00\) contributes mass \(1/20\) to factual cell \((A,Y)=(0,0)\), state \(10\) contributes masses \(9/20\) to cells \((0,1)\) and \((1,0)\), and state \(11\) contributes mass \(1/20\) to cell \((1,1)\). Thus all four factual cells equal (1). The benefit and harm coordinates are
\[
B=0,
\qquad
H=\pi_{10}=\frac9{10},
\tag{5}
\]
and the latent entropy is
\[
-2\frac1{20}\log\frac1{20}
-\frac9{10}\log\frac9{10}
=h\!\left(\frac9{10}\right)+\frac1{10}\log2
=\kappa^\dagger.
\tag{6}
\]
Equations (4)--(6), or directly \(\texttt{lem:factor-program-equivalence}\), therefore show
\[
\theta^\dagger\in
\Phi_3(\mathcal F_{3,\kappa^\dagger}(P^\dagger)).
\tag{7}
\]

We next prove that no two-state witness is possible at this budget. Consider any factual-compatible law with the coordinates in (2), and let \(J\) be its joint law of \((A,R)\). Since all response-type masses are nonnegative, \(B=0\) and \(H=9/10\) imply
\[
J(R=01)=0,
\qquad J(R=10)=\frac9{10},
\qquad J(R=00)+J(R=11)=\frac1{10}.
\tag{8}
\]
Consistency and the two diagonal factual cells give
\[
J(0,00)=p^\dagger_{00}=\frac1{20},
\qquad
J(1,11)=p^\dagger_{11}=\frac1{20}.
\tag{9}
\]
The two quantities in (9) already sum to the last quantity in (8). Nonnegativity therefore forces
\[
J(1,00)=J(0,11)=0.
\tag{10}
\]
Using the remaining factual cells and (10) now gives
\[
J(0,10)=p^\dagger_{01}=\frac9{20},
\qquad
J(1,10)=p^\dagger_{10}=\frac9{20}.
\tag{11}
\]
Consequently, (8)--(11) force the complete joint table
\[
J(0,00)=\frac1{20},\quad
J(0,10)=\frac9{20},\quad
J(1,10)=\frac9{20},\quad
J(1,11)=\frac1{20},
\tag{12}
\]
with every other cell equal to zero.

Suppose, toward a contradiction, that (12) has an exact product-mixture factorization with at most two positive-mass states. Write the state masses as \(\lambda_w\), the propensities as \(e_w\), and the conditional response probabilities as \(s_w(r)\). Positivity of \(J(0,00)\) produces a state \(w_0\) with \(\lambda_{w_0}s_{w_0}(00)>0\). Since
\[
0=J(1,00)=\sum_w\lambda_w e_w s_w(00),
\]
and every summand is nonnegative, \(e_{w_0}=0\). Likewise, positivity of \(J(1,11)\) produces a state \(w_1\) with \(\lambda_{w_1}s_{w_1}(11)>0\), while
\[
0=J(0,11)=\sum_w\lambda_w(1-e_w)s_w(11)
\]
forces \(e_{w_1}=1\). Thus \(w_0\neq w_1\). With at most two positive states these are all the states, and \(W\) determines \(A\). The observed law (1) is balanced, so
\[
\lambda_{w_0}=P^\dagger(A=0)=\frac12,
\qquad
\lambda_{w_1}=P^\dagger(A=1)=\frac12.
\]
Every such two-state factorization consequently has entropy
\[
-\frac12\log\frac12-\frac12\log\frac12=\log2
>\kappa^\dagger,
\tag{13}
\]
contradicting its membership in \(\mathcal F_{2,\kappa^\dagger}(P^\dagger)\). Hence
\[
\theta^\dagger\notin
\Phi_2(\mathcal F_{2,\kappa^\dagger}(P^\dagger)).
\tag{14}
\]

Finally, every two-state feasible tuple can be padded by a third zero-mass state; this changes neither its entropy, its factual cells, nor its benefit--harm image. Therefore
\[
\Phi_2(\mathcal F_{2,\kappa^\dagger}(P^\dagger))
\subseteq
\Phi_3(\mathcal F_{3,\kappa^\dagger}(P^\dagger)),
\]
and (7), (14) make the inclusion strict. The zero-pattern argument is the causal response-type embedding of the product-mixture support obstruction in \(\citet[Section V, Example 2 and Appendix A]{KumarLiElGamal2014}\); the information-theoretic obstruction is not claimed as new here, while the factual-compatible benefit--harm embedding has been verified explicitly above.

proposed.comparator_claim: Section V, Proposition 6 gives finite-joint-law common-entropy compression to at most \(2^{\min\{|\mathcal X|,|\mathcal Z|\}}-1\) states.
Section V, Proposition 8 gives the sharper two-state entropy minimizer when both variables are binary.
Section V, Example 2 and Appendix A exhibit the product-mixture support-pattern obstruction that the present response-type construction embeds causally.
A finite common-cause confounder d-separates treatment and response variables, and its entropy implies mutual-information restrictions used for scalar causal outer bounds.
Among several assumption regimes, factual probabilities alone give the unrestricted response-function benchmark for probabilities of causation.
Separate benefit and harm bounds are derived from two sensitivity parameters or a measured proxy.
Closed-form scalar interventional bounds are tight when the full nondegenerate finite confounder marginal \(\nu=P(U)\) is fixed and observed cells are positive.
Sharp symbolic nonparametric bounds are derived for benefit and related functionals without a Shannon-entropy budget.
Discrete causal queries reduce to finite polynomial programs with continuously refined valid outer bounds and epsilon-sharp scalar guarantees.
The causaloptim workflow automates tight symbolic bounds for linear response-function problems by vertex enumeration.
Likelihood-ordered covering collections yield finite-sample multinomial confidence regions with controlled coverage.
Criterion-defined identified sets admit consistency, rate, and confidence-region analysis under regularity conditions.
Breakdown frontiers for treatment-effect conclusions admit root-sample estimators and derivative-aware uniform confidence bands.

payload.tldr: Average effects conceal simultaneous benefit and harm, while existing low-entropy-confounding bounds often retain only mutual-information consequences and scalar targets. This note identifies the exact joint set \(\Theta_\kappa(P)\) over factual-compatible common-latent SCMs. Its support-cardinality elbow is exact: two positive latent states suffice for the no-individual-effect origin face, whereas three states suffice and are sometimes necessary for the full benefit--harm image. The note also gives the iff common-entropy threshold for origin entry, a full-support law where the mutual-information rule admits the origin too early, the zero-budget Frechet segment, the high-budget factual rectangle under treatment positivity, and a star kernel at intermediate budgets. Rank-free BH-CERT termination at zero weights or active entropy equality and the regular-versus-contact Hausdorff law remain open; exact multinomial whole-set coverage is retained only as a supporting set-mapping corollary.

project_justification.gap: JiangWeiKocaoglu2023 studies a common-cause graph and uses entropy-implied mutual-information restrictions for scalar causal bounds; Zhang2024 fixes the full finite confounder marginal \(\nu=P(U)\), assumes positive observed cells and nondegenerate \(U\), and derives scalar interventional bounds; Pena2023 and GabrielSachsJensen2024 bound benefit or harm under other restrictions. None identifies the joint benefit--harm plane when the confounder distribution is unknown and restricted only by \(\operatorname{Ent}_Q(U)\leq\kappa\), proves its exact two-versus-three-state support elbow, or supplies rank-free certification at zero latent masses or active entropy equality.
project_justification.niche: At the no-effect origin, exact feasibility is a binary common-entropy factorization problem and therefore needs only two positive latent states. Away from that face, the fixed joint law of treatment and the four-valued response type governs both factual compatibility and cross-world coordinates; its exact compression needs three states in general, and the balanced reverse-channel witness proves that the third state is not an artifact.
project_justification.fill: The project supplies an exact finite-factor map for the sharp joint set, proves a three-state representation for every binary factual law without treatment positivity, proves that three states are sometimes necessary, and pairs this with the exact two-state origin frontier and a full-support mutual-information false inclusion. It derives endpoint and star-kernel geometry on their stated positive-arm domains and isolates BH-CERT termination and entropy-contact inference as open rather than claimed deliverables.

sampling_model.overlap: The observed treatment probability \(p_1\) may lie anywhere in \([0,1]\) for the model fiber, the origin frontier, and the three-state reduction. The arm risk \(\mu_a=P(Y=1\mid A=a)\) is introduced only when \(P(A=a)>0\); endpoint and star-kernel formulas that use both arm risks retain treatment positivity. The analytic separation law has all four factual cells positive.

payload.related_work:
KumarLiElGamal2014 proves product-mixture results for arbitrary finite joint laws, not a causal model class. Its Proposition 6 gives the general fixed-joint-law cardinality bound used after forming the joint law of binary treatment and the four-valued response type; its Proposition 8 gives the sharper two-state bound when both observed variables are binary, which governs the no-effect origin. The three-state sharpness proposition is a factual-compatible causal embedding of the support-pattern obstruction in its Section V, Example 2 and Appendix A, not a claim that the information-theoretic obstruction is new. JiangWeiKocaoglu2023 uses a common-cause graph in which the finite confounder d-separates treatment and response variables; collapsing its finite confounder set into \(U\) yields the present nonparametric full-data conditional-exchangeability class after consistency is added, while this note replaces the mutual-information consequence by the exact entropy-constrained union. Zhang2024 fixes the full marginal \(
u=P(U)\), assumes positive observed cells and nondegenerate finite \(U\), and proves scalar interventional bounds. On the common domain, the present entropy class is the union of fixed-\(
u\) fibers over all finite \(
u\) with \(H(
u)\leq\kappa\); a fixed-\(

TianPearl2000 analyzes several regimes and supplies the factual-only unrestricted response-function benchmark used here; it is not summarized as only the rectangle. Pena2023 and GabrielSachsJensen2024 establish clinically motivated benefit or harm bounds under different restrictions. SachsJonzonSjolanderGabriel2022 and DuarteFinkelsteinKnoxMummoloShpitser2024 inform the response-function and certified-bounding architecture, while JonzonSachsGabriel2023 supplies causaloptim's polyhedral workflow as a computational contrast rather than a class that BH-CERT extends. ChafaiConcordet2009 supplies the exact multinomial coverage event, and ChernozhukovHongTamer2007, FangSantos2019, and MastenPoirier2020 motivate but do not settle entropy-contact Hausdorff inference.
payload.technical_internal_limitation: The fixed-joint-law compression is proved, including boundary factual laws, and the balanced reverse-channel witness proves that the full image genuinely needs three states at some budgets. The separate binary origin factorization and its diagonal causal completion need only two positive states. These population results do not close the computational singularity: no proof yet makes BH-CERT terminate with two-sided Hausdorff certificates at zero latent weights or active entropy equality without a rank condition, and no radial or KKT expansion has established the regular-versus-contact Hausdorff limit law.
payload.honest_scope: The paper's proved population support claim is the exact elbow: at most two positive states on the no-individual-effect origin face and at most three states, sometimes necessarily three, for the full benefit--harm image. The general Proposition 6 result is used only as fixed-joint-law compression, the Proposition 8 binary specialization only on the origin face, and the Example 2/Appendix A obstruction only through an explicit causal embedding. The three-state reduction itself allows \(p_1\in[0,1]\); formulas using both conditional arm risks retain \(0<p_1<1\), and no unproved boundary endpoint formula is asserted. BH-CERT termination at zero weights and entropy contact remains open, as does the exact contact-directional Hausdorff law. Finite-sample whole-set coverage is only the deterministic image of an imported exact multinomial coverage event and does not claim a new confidence-region method or optimal expected area.
